request.system: You are a senior clinical coder in an Australian public hospital with fifteen years of experience coding inpatient episodes in ICD-10-AM. You are careful, conservative, and you never invent a code you are not sure of the chapter for.

messages.content:
Code the episode of care below. The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed. Give the three-character ICD-10-AM category for the principal diagnosis.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary

Patient: 75-year-old male with history of tobacco abuse and metastatic p16 positive squamous cell carcinoma (SCC)

Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted with initial symptoms of swelling in the left neck followed by progressive hoarseness and dysphagia over a span of one to two months. A biopsy of the left neck node confirmed squamous cell carcinoma and the patient was later found to have pulmonary metastases. He required tracheostomy and gastrostomy placement for threatened airway obstruction and dysphagia, respectively. 

Treatment and Progression:
The patient was initially enrolled in a clinical trial comparing first-line EXTREME chemotherapy versus ipilimumab and nivolumab and was randomized to combination ipilimumab and nivolumab delivered concurrently every three weeks for four cycles. However, follow-up imaging at eight weeks showed progression of disease. The patient was then treated with ‘QUAD SHOT’ for palliation and delivered 3.7 Gy BID x 2 days (total dose 14.8 Gy) to gross disease. The patient continued through the third and fourth cycles of nivolumab and ipilimumab without breaks or delays. Radiation was delivered during the three-week time frame between immunotherapy cycles and he tolerated treatment well with minimal pain and noticeable improvement in the left neck mass. Repeat imaging showed continued decrease in size of all neck and most lung disease, with one lung nodule minimally increasing in size.

Outcome:
At the time of writing (10 months from initial diagnosis), the patient has completed a total of 14 cycles of ipilimumab and nivolumab on trial and is currently living with stable, asymptomatic disease. The patient continues to be followed up for response to treatment.
Diagnoses: [diagnosis section withheld]
Procedures:
- Biopsy of the left neck node
- Tracheostomy and gastrostomy placement 
- ‘QUAD SHOT’ for palliation 

Follow-up:
The patient continues to be followed up for response to treatment.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis needs a site, and the summary doesn't give a clear primary site. A p16-positive SCC with a neck node and hoarseness and dysphagia suggests an oropharyngeal primary, but the summary never names it. The conditions documented are metastatic SCC in a left neck node and in the lung, with an unknown primary.

ICD-10-AM coding rules for this situation:
- Secondary neoplasms (C77–C79) are coded as principal only when the primary is not being treated or is no longer present. Here the treatment is directed at the metastatic disease, and the primary site is not documented.
- When the primary site is unknown and the patient is treated for metastatic disease, the options are C77.0 (secondary neoplasm of lymph nodes of head, face and neck) or C80 (malignant neoplasm without specification of site / unknown primary).
- C80.0 is "malignant neoplasm, primary site unknown, so stated." It applies only if the record states the primary is unknown. The record doesn't say that.

Metastatic disease in the neck node and lung is the documented condition. The treatment (immunotherapy and palliative radiotherapy) is directed at the nodal and pulmonary metastases, and the tracheostomy and gastrostomy were for airway obstruction and dysphagia caused by the neck disease. The neck node is the first presenting site and the main focus of the admission, so the category is C77, secondary and unspecified malignant neoplasm of lymph nodes.

CODE: C77
